chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Faith has four pillars: reliance upon Allah, delegating the matter to Allah, contentment with the decree of Allah, and submission to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars of faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from his father Imam al-Baqir and ultimately to Imam Ali, defines the spiritual architecture of faith through four interrelated states of the heart. It emphasizes that true Iman is not merely belief but a comprehensive surrender (Taslim) and contentment (Rida) that transforms divine decree into a source of inner peace. This framework is central to Shia theological understanding of the believer's relationship with the Divine Will.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, from his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The Emān has four pillars for it – the reliance upon Allahazwj, and delegating the matter to Allahazwj, and the pleasure with the Judgement of Allahazwj, and the submission to the Command of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali form al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah from his father (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘Belief has four corner (stones): They are trust in Allah, having Allah as the person in charge of one’s affairs, to agree with the decision of Allah and to submit to the command of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’”
